## UNGM Registration Requirements

Registration as a vendor with UNGM is required to do business with the UN.(no content)The registration process on UNGM encompasses three registration levels, and for each registration level, suppliers will be required to fill out a registration form.

Key requirements for registration include:

- Acknowledgment of the UN Supplier Code of Conduct
- Provide the supplier's name as it appears on the company's Certificate of Incorporation or other legal documentation
- During the registration process, the license number is used to identify the supplier records as unique. It is best to provide the number that appears on the Certificate of Incorporation. If the supplier does not have a business license number, they may provide another official identification number such as the tax ID number.
- If an original document is not in English, suppliers are required to upload a translated document translated by an external independent certified translator

## Supplier Verification

Being registered on UNGM means that the details of your company is part of the database of potential vendors. Once any of the UN organizations confirm your registration, your company's profile will be visible to all UN staff when searching for vendors.

## International Development Banks

The registration requirements differ significantly among international development banks. World Bank does not require registration for participation in the procurement process. World Bank financed contracts implement prequalification procedures in the process to create shortlists. These procedures are handled on a case-by-case basis. However, in order to receive a contract award they must be "Approved", which requires completion of a Vendor Registration form, meeting all eligibility requirements and providing all required documentation.

SECTION 4: PROCUREMENT TENDER TYPES GLOSSARY
================================================================================

ICB (INTERNATIONAL COMPETITIVE BIDDING)
- Scope: International participation permitted
- Minimum Contract Value: $1M-$10M typical (varies by organization)
- Eligibility: Companies from development bank member countries
- Advertising Period: Typically 6 weeks minimum
- Advertisement Method: Official portals, donor websites, international media
- Procurement Method: Full competitive sealed bidding
- Application: Major works, goods, and consultancy contracts
- Price Range: Higher value contracts typically use ICB
- Documentation: Comprehensive procurement notices published

NCB (NATIONAL COMPETITIVE BIDDING)
- Scope: National companies primarily eligible
- Geographic Restriction: Usually country-specific or regional
- Competitive Process: Formal competitive bidding required
- Documentation: Published tender notices locally and nationally
- Eligibility: Nationals/residents of implementing country
- Process: Usually faster than ICB
- Foreign Participation: May be allowed depending on organization policy
- Value Range: Often used for smaller to medium contracts
- Administration: Implementing country responsible

RFP (REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL)
- Format: Detailed requirements and evaluation criteria provided
- Submission: Written proposals required
- Evaluation: Non-price factors important (quality, experience, approach)
- Typical Use: Consulting services, complex technical projects, capacity building
- Timeline: Usually longer than sealed bidding for evaluation
- Proposal Components: Technical proposal + financial proposal required
- Quality Emphasis: Best-value selection rather than lowest price

RFQ (REQUEST FOR QUOTATION)
- Format: Simple price quotation request
- Minimum Participants: Usually 3-5 quotes sought
- Response Time: Quick turnaround (1-2 weeks typical)
- Evaluation: Primarily price-based
- Use Cases: Standard goods, routine services, commodity procurement
- Documentation: Simplified compared to ITB/RFP
- Value Threshold: Often used for smaller contracts

ITB (INVITATION TO BID)
- Scope: International sealed competitive bidding
- Mechanism: Detailed tender documents with bid forms provided
- Response: Submitted in sealed envelopes per specifications
- Evaluation: Predetermined evaluation criteria applied
- Price Component: Critical evaluation factor
- Participation: Broader international participation
- Transparency: Formal bid opening process
- Contract Value: Wide range depending on organization

CONSULTANCY SERVICES PROCUREMENT
- Talent Types: Individual consultants and consulting firms
- Selection Methods: CV review, interviews, qualifications assessment
- Advertisement: Portal listings and notifications
- Rates: Daily, monthly, or fixed price arrangements
- Duration: Short-term assignments to long-term engagements
- Specializations: Technical, management, training, research
- Geographic Focus: International and national consultants
- Experience Requirements: Sector expertise, credentials important

FRAMEWORK AGREEMENTS
- Duration: Usually 1-3 years
- Pricing: Pre-negotiated rates
- Call-off Process: Specific tasks ordered as needed
- Supplier Base: Multiple pre-qualified providers
- Flexibility: Allows rapid procurement of known requirements
- Use Cases: IT services, maintenance, professional services
- Lock-in Pricing: Reduces cost uncertainty

   NCB (national competitive bidding) for local work. Home country location
   not required, but local presence in Africa/target regions helpful.

   type. UNDP/WFP have e-procurement portals for payment tracking. Payment
